New update is fantastic, hope for more to come!. I have been an off and on user of Focus for a long time. The latest update adds much needed UI love, and works so much better, especially on my iPad. Great work!

One area I think could use some love is the Apple Shortcuts. I can only speak for myself here but being able to add new tasks using Apple shortcuts would vastly improve my workflow. For example, it would allow me to create a shortcut to import all my daily tasks from Reminders. If I had a wishlist the two shortcuts would be “Create task with title and date” and “Filter/find existing tasks” to complete the “search and sync” features using shortcuts. 

Additionally, a game changing feature would be the ability to automatically trigger the app to change the OS level Focus modes when starting/stopping sessions (or maybe just trigger shortcuts instead). For now I use Apple shortcuts to start DND at the same time as starting a Focus timer in the app, but I would love to be able to exit DND during breaks and automatically resume DND when my break is over. 

Overall this is a great update and I love seeing it! The simplicity of this app makes it one of the best, and with some of the features above I think it would stand above the rest for me and instant 5 star. 

I am going to resubscribe for now. I know you can’t promise anything but I wanted to be sure to share my thoughts. 

Keep up the great work!

Asks for money immediately after first startup. I’m always leery of apps that offer in-app purchases. I appreciate that software developers need to be paid - I am one, and I follow a business model that allows free trials and licenses. But it’s a big red flag for me when my first experience with an app is a popup screen shilling for subscriptions. This one lists features I would consider basic- the kind I downloaded it fo -asking for $39.99/year to give me just a few additional features I don’t already have from other free and paid apps. 

Always look at old reviews: they may be irrelevant to you, they may be outdated, but you can learn a lot from reading the complaints and responses. Looking at the promoted reviews, you may see what I saw, that the developer deflects criticisms and offers weak answers to issues. 

Example: when told that Dark Mode should be a built-in feature, not an in-app purchase, the developer directed the user to iOS built-in dark mode. As if a photosensitive user hadn’t tried that before! And maybe they discovered that Dark Mode on iOS causes other applications to be rendered less accessible due to invisible icons. (I’m looking at you 1Password and IntelliJ.) A good user experience for photosensitive users must be built into an app with care. I can always tell when a software company hasn’t actually tried to use their own software features, because they wouldn’t tolerate them. Many people want Dark Mode, so just give it to them, and give them other reasons to pay add-on prices. To suggest otherwise is to show contempt for your prospective client base.

Great app!. I am a too lazy of a person to write any review, but I like this app and wanted to share some information and suggestion about the app. 

As a law student, I have been feeling anxious, uncertain if I am putting in enough hours for my school work, and this app does a great job letting me track how long I did the work each day. I like that I can adjust a number of minutes for each session In because most of apps only provide pomodoro style 25 minutes as an option. Also, I love that I could have the app fill the whole screen so I could start it again. Before using this function, I always missed hitting the start button again that I ended up deleting similar types of apps because of imprecise hours tracked. 

If I may make some suggestions- it would be nice if I could label how many hours I spent on each task. Just a chunk of hours logged only gives me an idea that I did something, but looking back, j don't know on which task I spent my time. Also, a stick or pie graph that shows how many hours I focused on each different task would make this app the greatest. I have been looking for one but there's none that has those functions. 

Thank you for this app and please keep up the great work!

reviews.text:
4.5 stars - minor improvements would make it perfect.. I gave this 5 stars but there are just a few minor improvements I would love to see that would make it a true 5/5 for me:

-Ability to create custom lists. Not all tasks that I add to Focus are the same. The bulk of it is my daily productivity usage - the tasks I work on as part of my job, which I take straight from my OmniFocus planner. But I also like to use Focus for my morning routine. I’m ADHD and getting out of the house on time is more challenging than it is for most people. Focus is a great help for me in the morning, by setting timers for the basic things - shower, breakfast, planning my day, etc. - it forces me to keep on schedule. Most people take this for granted, but with ADHD, the mornings can be the hardest because the meds haven’t kicked in yet, so having a dedicated “morning routine” list, as an example, would be great.

-The ability to set default session and break times unique to the above custom lists. My morning routine session timer may be 15-20 minutes. My workday timer might be 45. Would be great to be able to set different defaults for each. 

-Repeatable tasks. Quite a few of the tasks on my list are things I do every day. It would be nice to set them to repeat. 

These three features would be amazing, but their lack does not take away from the fact that this app is awesome. It does just what the name says, keeps me focused, and as importantly, makes it much more likely that I will take breaks, which I frequently neglect to do. It makes me more productive in the end, less stressed, and more balanced. Wonderful app.

reviews.text:
Good, can be better. Overall nice simple design and set of features, and haven’t seen any bugs. With some changes and additions I think it can be the go-to app for Pomodoro. Having Watch support is a huge bonus as it’s very useful to have access to that when I’m doing one thing or another. I’m using it on a Watch 4 and iPhone

Watch
 The Watch app doesn’t work unless it’s connected to the phone, please add an untethered mode that syncs when the phone is in range again. 

 The end session notification is much too subtle. It’s so easy to miss that I can’t use it, for example when playing the piano you don’t notice the sounds or tapping. Developer, use the timer app as a good example, that is impossible to miss. 

iPhone
 Main screen swiping is a little confusing, but that’s a small nit. Overall looks clean and nice. 

First, please add HealthKit integration. It’s known that focused concentration is a great way to stave off cognitive decline as we age, and important at any age. HealthKit is the best way to track this data, just use “Focus” as the entry tag.

The main complaint is the Pro subscription model. That’s the business model the developer decided on as their right, but I think it’s a mistake. This is a really simple bit of functionality, paying a continuous subscription doesn’t make any sense to me. One reason is that people who Pomodoro typically have a set routine with it. Most creatives seem to max out at 4-6 sessions/day, and do it every day. It would be nice to track this but hardly necessary, because it’s habitual. My point is that I believe a single paid in-app purchase (up to say $10) makes much more sense than a subscription - personally I’ll probably not use it and delete until/if such pricing becoming available, because there are other free apps that have the same functionality (but this one is overall cleaner and I’d prefer using it). 

So developer, my suggestion is to add the few Watch improvements above, and to reconsider the business model.

Useful but why a subscription?. I understand the need for continued support but other similar or even more useful apps work without structure. First useful, reliable Complication I've ever encountered. This is primarily about the new Focus watchOS 2 app. I've been trying a whole bunch of third party apps in hopes of finding a solid complication, and all of them either aren't very useful or work unreliably.

Not so with Focus. Having a pomodoro timer on my wrist that I can quickly refer to is excellent and, best of all, it works very well! There's occasionally a bit of lag syncing back to the phone app, but what's important is that it actually *syncs* and the Complication accurately shows where I'm at in my pomodoro interval.

I'm very impressed with it. Keeping it on my watch face for sure.

It's a timer?. App has no function other than being identical to clock app timer? Anyone can set timer for 25 minutes to finish a task. Waste of money. Nothing can be done to improve app because it is pointless to start out with.

I use this version to complement the Mac version. Far and away best pomodoro app on the Mac. I like this version on the iPad. I wish this one had dark mode like on Mac...that color scheme looks much cooler.

No graphs?. I like how it tracks time spent on each task, but the presentation of statistics is too scattered to make sense of in a hurry. It would be great to have some kind of line graph--either for total work time per day, or according to tags that could be assigned to multiple tasks.
I'd also like an option to hide the numerals from the countdown timer while it's running. The timer is less distracting if it's graphical only.

Yes. It works.. Works great across all platforms. Syncs in real time. I can move seamlessly between devices and watch while on a task. Well done. 

Wish List: integration with reminders and calendar. Folders for tasks. Hierarchical task structure. 

Keep going!

Need time tracking broken down by tasks. The app works quite well, but would be much more useful if the focused sessions can be broken down by individual tasks. 

There probably should be a tab that will tell you how many focused sessions you have completed for that one particular task.

Amazing!. This is a well-thought out app and actually helps me stay more productive! I'd love to see how exactly the development of this app continues! In my opinion, I'd love to see an "Import from Reminders" option because I tend to keep all of my to-dos there and move them to Focus when I want to work on them that specific day.
Love it. Syncs across devices and looks great, which is important for a software you'll be looking at many times a day! Features feel nicely balanced and, well, in focus.

Disappointed for the price - But Customer Service WIN. Original review: I don't know why the ability to create a task list is included in this app. The number of times a task is repeated is not recorded. Nor is the task listed in the activity log. Instead it just says "Focus Session" over and over. This makes it impossible to record how much time is spent on each task, a feature I was looking for in addition to knowing when I completed a session. The time each session ends is the feature that motivated me to get Focus, but in the balance I would rather know how much time I spent on a certain task than when each individual session ended. Also, it does not seem possible to switch between tasks at the end of a session without marking the current task as "done." I am VERY disappointed as this is one of the few apps I've actually spent money on... And it feels like something of a waste. Especially since this app is remarkably good in most other ways. If tasks were integrated into the activity log or a simple session counter on each task were added, I would give this app five stars without hesitation.

Update:
I wrote in with the suggestions listed above a received a personal email than addressed my concerns. Because I was handled so courteously (even to the point of providing the proper link when I asked about how to get a refund), I'm going to stick with Focus. Also, Jan said that they plan to improve the statistics with an update in a couple of months. Will wait it out with an inferior pomodoro app (not Focus) and hopefully start really using Focus in Jan/Feb.

Terrible. Don't waste your $6.99. I found this featured app while searching for watch apps so one would expect that this app is actually built around the watch. Nope. I'm not even sure how you screw something so simple up. You tell the watch to start a 25 minute timer. 2 hours later, the timer still has 6 minutes left. How do you screw up a simple timer in 2015. Unbelievable. Getting a refund.

reviews.text: Nice Clean and Easy Focus Timer. This is easy to use, does help you focus, and syncs well. I wish the tasks were more integrated with the focus periods in the history view (instead of separate disconnected views) so it would be far more useful.

Useless on Watch. There is no notification on the watch. If I need to check my watch every few seconds it completely defeats the purpose of using this as a timer for focusing on a task. Reinstalled and adjusted all settings after requesting support and still no watch notification.

reviews.text:
This is the "Queue" of tasks I've been looking for!. Great, solid approach. Works great. Syncs fast. On a lot of platforms. Awesome stuff. 

Requests:
1. Show active task on Apple Watch with option to complete
2. Show list of upcoming tasks in another view. Tap and hold on one to make active. 
3. Show active task with option to complete in Notification Center of iOS.
Productivity Boost!. This is the first Pomodoro app that has fully clicked with me. I can make a session as long or short as I need and the handoff between iPhone and Mac works seamlessly.
Does not integrate with work tasks!. I thought Focus would use task list from iPhone based on description, it doesn't.

Improves my Productivity. When you really have to focus on a task, this is the app to help you get it done. Based on the Pomodoro method, instead of working for hours and hours on end, you do work, take a break, do work, take a break, etc. By default, you would work for 25 minutes and take a 5 minute break. After four sessions are complete, you are rewarded with a longer 20 minute break. Additionally, you can keep a list of your tasks needed to be done, check them off and view a history of the tasks and sessions you’ve completed. 

This app works great on iPhone and ever better on the Apple Watch. I can use the Apple Watch app to quickly see how much time is remaining in my session/break and also pause the timer.

Helps Me Focus and Get Work Done. If anyone knows about the animal personality tests, I am an otter. I have so much trouble staying on tasks. A YouTube video or Pinterest notification will have me gone, and before I know it, my emails are backed up! This app helps me to knock my work out and then I get rewarded during the breaks to do what I want. It's a good mix of work and break and now I'm getting all my work done and not stressed!
App does not sync to the Watch or iCloud! Enough said!. App does not sync to the Watch or iCloud! Enough said! $5.00!

reviews.text: Simple productivity timer that works as advertised. I love that this app is simple and the gui is very clean. This does exactly what it is supposed to. I’m looking forward to trying the Apple Watch app as soon as I receive my new watch.

Buggy💔. There is a critical bug in the app. The bug will erase all finished sessions records when you operate it on your Apple Watch. It would be a good app if it works. Hi developer, test before release it! 💔💔💔
